summary.text: Nunn is the Republican incumbent, first elected to Iowa's 3rd District in 2022 after four years in the Iowa House and four in the Iowa Senate. A colonel in the Air Force Reserve, he previously worked on cybersecurity policy at the White House National Security Council. He serves on the House Financial Services and Agriculture committees.

paragraphs.text: Nunn is a sixth-generation Iowan who, according to his official biography, was raised on Des Moines' east side in a family of public school teachers, nurses, and farmers and attended Southeast Polk High School. Wikipedia gives his birth date as May 4, 1979.

He earned a bachelor's degree in political science and international relations from Drake University in 2002, a master's degree in military operational art and science from the U.S. Air Force Air Command and Staff College, and a master's degree from Cambridge University in 2007.

Nunn served almost two decades in the U.S. Air Force as an airborne intelligence officer, deploying three times to the Middle East after 9/11, according to his official biography; he remains a colonel in the Air Force Reserve.

His civilian career has included work as an adjunct professor of cybersecurity and national policy at Drake University, director of business development at SimSpace Corporation, chief operations officer and national counterintelligence officer with the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, and director of cybersecurity policy and engagement on the White House National Security Council.
Nunn served in the Iowa House of Representatives from 2015 to 2019 and in the Iowa Senate from 2019 to 2023.
He won the 3rd District seat in November 2022 by defeating incumbent Democrat Cindy Axne, 50.3% to 49.6%, and was re-elected in 2024 with about 52% of the vote.

In the 119th Congress he sits on the House Financial Services Committee, where he is vice chairman of the national security and illicit finance subcommittee, as well as the House Agriculture Committee and the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party.
According to his official biography, Nunn lives in Ankeny with his wife, Kelly; they have six children, two of them adopted.
